title: ScopeGuard research checkpoints
provenance: Original ScopeGuard research prompts and systematic scenario variations, informed by OWASP WSTG, ASVS, API Security, MASVS/MASTG, GenAI guidance and PortSwigger Web Security Academy. References are background at area level, not one-to-one standard mappings. This is not a universal checklist used by all top researchers, a certification, or an exhaustive security assessment.
limits: Catalog entries are not executed tests, testing permission, confirmed bugs, or promised earnings. Applicability depends on actual features and current program rules. Some areas require specialist tools and controlled environments.

categories.title: Permission and research boundaries
categories.prerequisites: Current permission for the exact asset and method; owned test identities where needed. Use local synthetic fixtures when an operation could change data, spend money, or affect availability.
categories.evidence: Official policy source, read time, exact wording needed for the decision, and unresolved conditions. A listing never supplies permission.

categories.prerequisites: Current permission for the exact asset and method; owned test identities where needed. Use local synthetic fixtures when an operation could change data, spend money, or affect availability.
categories.evidence: Relevant authorized source/configuration or an expressly permitted owned-account observation; exact version and context, expected behavior, a safe baseline, and minimal redacted evidence.

categories.title: Business workflow integrity
categories.prerequisites: Current permission for the exact asset and method; owned test identities where needed. Use local synthetic fixtures when an operation could change data, spend money, or affect availability.
categories.evidence: Relevant authorized source/configuration or an expressly permitted owned-account observation; exact version and context, expected behavior, a safe baseline, and minimal redacted evidence.

checks.title: Enforce required workflow steps on the server.
Reject state transitions that skip mandatory approval.
Bind approval to the exact item and version reviewed.
Revoke an approval when material input changes.
Keep canceled operations from being completed later.
Require separate privileges for proposing and approving sensitive changes.
Prevent users from approving their own request where separation is required.
Enforce per-user limits using trusted identity data.
Apply organization limits across alternate client channels.
Handle negative quantities according to business rules.
Handle zero quantities without granting unintended benefits.
Bound monetary and quantity precision before calculations.
Recalculate authoritative totals on the server.
Keep promotional eligibility independent of client-supplied labels.
Prevent expired offers from being redeemed through stale requests.
Validate ownership when transferring credits or entitlements.
Keep trial conversion from restoring already consumed benefits.
Protect administrative workflow overrides with explicit privilege.
Model abuse cases with synthetic balances and harmless objects.
Distinguish unexpected business behavior from a security boundary violation.

categories.title: AI instructions and untrusted content
categories.prerequisites: Current permission for the exact asset and method; owned test identities where needed. Use local synthetic fixtures when an operation could change data, spend money, or affect availability.
categories.evidence: Synthetic instructions and canary data, model/configuration identity, observed tool behavior, and a benign baseline.

checks.title: Keep retrieved text separate from higher-trust application instructions.
Treat uploaded documents as data rather than operational commands.
Keep tool-returned text from changing the agent's authorization scope.
Preserve user intent when a web page requests an unrelated action.
Prevent quoted instructions from silently becoming executable directives.
Keep hidden document text from overriding the requested task.
Handle conflicting tool output with an explicit trust policy.
Restrict model-selected destinations to independently validated resources.
Prevent generated text from being executed as application code implicitly.
Validate structured model outputs before consuming their fields.
Apply output encoding when rendering generated HTML-like content.
Keep prompts from being the sole enforcement of access controls.
Separate public prompt disclosure from disclosure of actual secrets.

categories.title: Evidence, validation, and reporting
categories.prerequisites: Current permission for the exact asset and method; owned test identities where needed. Use local synthetic fixtures when an operation could change data, spend money, or affect availability.
categories.evidence: Minimal reproducible evidence, permission record, negative control, impact reasoning, redaction, and the remaining validation questions.
